title: Portable sandbox cookbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working cookbook for a portable, reproducible sandbox used in short hands-on codelabs, 1:1 integrations, and field demos. The goal: a single artifact devs can run locally or in ephemeral cloud instances that closely mirrors Redwood hosted behavior (routing, token use, telemetry) without heavy infra.

High-level constraints / principles (opinionated)
- zero-cloud-ops friction: single script to get started (mac/linux)
- hermetic presets: seeded prompts, short token-limited examples, small fixture data
- telemetry light-touch: local traces emitted to a file + optional upload hook for QA
- predictable performance profile: simulate latency/bandwidth to test fallthroughs
- small surface area: focus on SDK usage patterns (init, streaming, error handling, retries) not full infra

Quick start (target 2–5 minutes)
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sandbox-presets.git && cd sandbox-presets
2) ./scripts/quick-boot.sh --mode=local --preset=hello-redwood
3) open http://localhost:8080 (mini UI) or run ./bin/run-sample --example hello-red
4) Try the three quick checks: token readout, streaming echo, failure-injection retry

Minimal environment (what quick-boot creates)
- docker-compose (single container) OR single-node node process with an in-memory mock runtime
- sample API key: sandbox-xxxx (expires on host restart)
- seeded prompts in /fixtures/prompt-sets/hello.json (3 variants)
- telemetry file: ./logs/sandbox-trace.log

Micro-codelabs (templates)
- Lab A: Hello-Red (5–10 min)
  - learning goal: SDK init, basic text.generate call, inspect token/cost metadata
  - steps: init, send short instruction, parse response, validate token fields
  - failure mode: 401 -> show ephemeral key refresh flow (./bin/refresh-key)
  - checklist: success if response returned and tokens_consumed > 0

- Lab B: Prompt riff + deterministic eval (15–20 min)
  - learning goal: prompt engineering loop and gating via prompt set regression tests
  - steps: run ./bin/prompt-riff --seed fixtures/prompt-sets/marketing.json; run eval harness ./bin/eval-set --gold fixtures/gold/marketing-v1.json
  - teach: how to pin model version, how to interpret subtle output regressions
  - artifact: small HTML report in ./out/eval-marketing.html

- Lab C: Streaming and fallbacks (10–15 min)
  - learning goal: consume streaming responses and implement safe fallback to chunked polling when stream fails
  - steps: run ./bin/stream-test --simulate-drop=0.15 ; implement client-side fallback using --poll-on-failure flag
  - success: UI shows streaming tokens and recovers to full response on drop

Failure & fallback heuristics (opinionated list)
- transient 5xx (<= 20% of requests): retry with exponential backoff, up to 3 attempts, then fallback to smaller model variant (preset: tiny-compat)
- stream disconnect: resume attempt once, then fall back to polling endpoint with cached prompt prefix
- auth token invalid: attempt local refresh, if refresh fails open step-by-step link to reset in console UI
- latency spike: detect p95 > 2s for >10s window -> show degrade banner and switch to prioritized low-latency preset

Observability (local-first)
- logs: structured JSON lines in ./logs/sandbox-trace.log (timestamp, request_id, route, duration_ms, tokens)
- traces: mini-xray format included (span annotations in log lines)
- lightweight UI: mini dashboard at /_sandbox/metrics showing last 100 requests with flamebar view
- sample query to reproduce: curl -s localhost:8080/_sandbox/metrics | jq .last_100

Presets & config (files)
- presets/ (yaml): hello-redwood.yaml, latency-stress.yaml, privacy-airgapped.yaml
- fixtures/: prompt sets + small documents (max 2MB total)
- dev.env (template): REDWOOD_API_KEY=sandbox-xxxx SANDBOX_MODE=local DEBUG_TELEMETRY=1

Developer onboarding checklist (for the person running the lab)
- [ ] pull repo and run quick-boot.sh locally (validate startup logs)
- [ ] run Lab A and confirm token consumption counter increments
- [ ] run Lab C and simulate stream drop -> validate fallback works
- [ ] create one GitHub issue with reproduction steps if anything fails

Known rough edges / TODOs (explicit)
- make quick-boot work on M1 without docker (current edge-case failure on homebrew sqlite)
- reduce fixture size further (some demos timeout on constrained CI runners)
- document clear clean-up steps for ephemeral tokens (some users keep long-running keys)
- add Windows quickstart script (PR welcome)

Performance knobs to expose in 2nd pass
- per-request simulated_cpu_ms (to mimic busy GPUs)
- windowed latency injection (to test degrade banners)
- configurable KV cache hit-rate (affects warm-start response times)

Teaching notes for facilitators
- keep to 3 core learning objectives (init, prompt loop, fallback)
- avoid deep infra topics in the first 15 minutes; emphasize SDK ergonomics
- when participants hit auth/token issues: guide them through quick refresh rather than re-issuing keys
- collect feedback via tiny form on the mini UI (POST /_sandbox/feedback)

Unresolved questions (for eng-developer-experience backlog)
- should we include a pre-seeded small-benchmark harness for token pricing comparisons across presets? (ENG-4380)
- desired retention / upload policy for telemetry when users opt to share traces for debugging?
- standard naming convention for presets across product teams (dedicated vs hosted semantics)

Quick links (commands + reference)
- Start local sandbox: ./scripts/quick-boot.sh --mode=local
- Run a single example without UI: ./bin/run-sample --example prompt-riff
- Force stream drop: ./bin/stream-test --simulate-drop=0.25
- Eval harness: ./bin/eval-set --report out/report.html --preset hello-redwood
- Telemetry tail: tail -f ./logs/sandbox-trace.log | jq -c . | sed -n '1,200p'

Notes-to-self (short)
- demo at next onboarding session: include latency tuning slide + two live failures
- ask SRE for small CI runner with 2GB RAM to validate the tiny preset
- rename hello-redwood -> hello-runtime in next pass (less product-y)

End.
